reasoning_content:
The dry run is still showing the "Missing from lock file" error, but it's also running the prepare script because the package is already installed in the workspace. The real issue is that `npm ci` in the Docker container is failing before node_modules exists — specifically during the prepare phase.

The dry-run error might be misleading since it runs prepare even though the install itself succeeded. I should test this the same way the Dockerfile does: copy the manifests to a temp directory and run `npm ci` there without the prepare script interfering.

action.command: rm -rf /tmp/npcitest && mkdir -p /tmp/npcitest && cp /workspace/01-frontend/package.json /workspace/01-frontend/package-lock.json /tmp/npcitest/ && for w in shared shell mfe-fp mfe-kp mfe-mp mfe-verwaltungsakt mfe-vp mfe-ws mfe1 mfe-ewm; do mkdir -p /tmp/npcitest/$w && cp /workspace/01-frontend/$w/package.json /tmp/npcitest/$w/; done && cd /tmp/npcitest && timeout 300 docker run --rm -v /tmp/npcitest:/w -w /w node:20-bookworm sh -c "HUSKY=0 npm ci 2>&1 | tail -8; echo CI_EXIT=\$?"
